newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian farmers block roads in tax protest.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian farmers block roads in tax protest.

text.p: Hungarian farmers protesting against tax changes blocked roads with thousands of tractors, ploughs and trucks across the country on Monday, police said.
The protests at 70 points delayed traffic for hours and organisers pledged to continue with them for at least two more days unless the government undid all the tax changes.

"We will not even talk to the government (about ending the protests) until all the new laws are suspended," Zsuzsa Sinkovicz, a member of the organising committee, said at a roadblock in the central Hungarian farm town of Kiskoros.
The farmers are protesting at the end of an exemption from social security contributions as of January 1 and new requirements to provide documents for taxation purposes.
National police spokeswoman Eva Kiss said about 4,200 vehicles and up to 7,000 people took part in the demonstrations in eight of Hungary's 19 counties, mostly in the less developed eastern half.
Kiss said that there were no incidents although cars had to line up several kilometres at some locations.
In Kiskoros, the centre of the protest, one of the main roads to Budapest was blocked by 500 vehicles forming a five km (three mile) long line. It took hours for cars to get to the next village.
Traffic on Highway 5 which links the Balkans and Turkey to western Europe was also delayed.
Highway 3, a western link, was blocked at Gyongyos, while cars had to line up for several kilometres on Highway 4, a key east-west route, Hungarian radio reported.

Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said earlier that the government was prepared to modify the new tax scheme but would not reinstate the social security exemptions for farmers or eliminate requirements to document expenses.
Making an exception would create unequal taxes for farmers and non-farmers and would jeopardise Hungary's finances while the documentation is needed to avoid abuse, Medgyessy said.
Farmers said the government was trying to balance its books on their backs.
"Gyula, don't try to recover from us the billions your government wasted," one placard taped to the top of a tractor said, referring to Prime Minister Gyula Horn.
Another placard said: "We want to farm, not do book keeping."
